card: Russian has three passives. A short participle for a result (perfective): **Дом постро́ен.** A **-ся** verb for a process or a habit (imperfective): **Дом стро́ится.** **Здесь продаю́тся биле́ты.** And, most often in speech, no passive at all: the **они́** form with no subject: **Здесь стро́ят дом.** **Меня́ зову́т А́нна.**

sections.body: English uses *is done* everywhere. Russian prefers active sentences, especially the subjectless **они́** form. Keep the real passives for writing and for results.

sections.title: Who did it
sections.body: The doer goes in the instrumental: **Дом был постро́ен рабо́чими.** **Рома́н чита́ют миллио́ны люде́й**: in speech, just make the doer the subject.

sections.title: The -ся passive is imperfective only
sections.body: **Дом стро́ится** (*is being built*) is fine. For a perfective passive use the participle: **Дом постро́ен**, not ~~Дом постро́ился~~.

mistakes.why: The doer of a passive is in the instrumental, with no preposition.
A perfective **-ся** verb isn't a passive: make the doer the subject.

examples.en: The house was built last year.
A new school is being built here.

examples.ru: Рома́н был переведён на два́дцать языко́в.
examples.en: The novel was translated into twenty languages.
